title: Stepped commit thresholds with auto-thresholding and rerank bucket pricing
creator: Elena Martinez
description:
Objective: Design and validate a stepped per-vector commitment model that auto-adjusts thresholds based on observed batch sizes and introduces a separate rerank 'bucket' price to better align cost with compute and latency impact. The goal is to: (1) preserve predictable unit economics for enterprise buyers with committed volumes, (2) deliver meaningful volume discounts for batched vector workloads, and (3) avoid regressive revenue for small- to mid-size customers that use high-frequency low-volume rerank calls.

Scope: Pricing model design, billing prototype logic, experiments for conversion uplift, contract language for commitments, and QSA notes for enterprise security/legal review. Implementation will require work from pricing PM, billing engineers (ingest + usage pipeline), experiments/data-science, and customer success to recruit pilot accounts.

Approach & key design decisions: 
- Stepped tiers: define small set of commit tiers (e.g., 100M / 500M / 2B vectors) with fixed per-vector rates inside tiers to simplify quoting and billing. Tiers chosen to match observed 80/20 distribution from usage histogram.
- Auto-thresholding: server-side heuristic that converts a customer's rolling 30-day effective batch size distribution into an "active threshold" used to grant transient discounting for short-term spikes without requiring a formal commitment change. This avoids forcing customers to over-commit but still captures volume economics.
- Rerank buckets: split reranking calls into separate price buckets (low, medium, high) based on input candidate set size and whether rerank uses cross-encoder scoring. Rationale: rerankers increase compute non-linearly vs simple embedding lookups.
- Per-vector rounding & billing granularity: bill to 1K-vector granularity for hosted API to reduce billing noise and per-request overhead. Ensure rounding rules are transparent in contract language.
- Safety valves & fallbacks: conservative rollout behind feature flag; default is opt-in for customers during pilot. Add ceiling on auto-discount to avoid sustained underpricing while model telemetry stabilizes.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Complexity vs transparency: stairs are simpler to explain to sales but lose some efficiency compared to continuous per-vector pricing. Chose stepped tiers to improve enterprise sales predictability.
- Auto-threshold risk: helps customers but may be gamed by bursty traffic — we limit by 30-day rolling window and cap discount rate.
- Rerank granularity: more buckets yield tighter cost alignment but complicate billing; start with 3 buckets and expand if needed.

Success metrics (experiment & pilot): 
- Conversion rate lift for mid-market/enterprise trials when offered stepped commit discounts (target +12% of quotes accepted).
- Net revenue retention impact: measured by committed customers + usage uplift vs baseline.
- Effective ARPU and margin per vector across buckets.
- Fraud/gaming signals: abnormal daily variance in batch patterns or repeated threshold changes.
- SLOs: no measurable change in 99th percentile latency for rerank endpoints during pilot.

Rollout plan: 
1) Finalize tier boundaries and rates (this ticket) by 2026-03-20.
2) Billing prototype & usage pipeline changes (ENG) — feature-flagged, internal testing: 2 sprints (ENG estimate ~8).
3) Small pilot with 3 anchor customers (CS to recruit) for 8 weeks. Monitor metrics with dashboard.
4) Iterate and expand to open opt-in for committed customers.

Compliance & QSA notes: document changes to billing pipeline, customer-facing SKUs, and sample contract language for the Security Questionnaire. Provide an expectation map for audit logs showing commit tiers, threshold history, and billing reasons.

comments: 2026-02-21 — Initial spike analysis: DS ran histograms over 18 months of embedding usage; 85% of accounts are under 50M vectors/month but top 3 customers account for ~60% of total volume.
2026-02-25 — Finance sync: agreed on target margin floor per tier. Need to validate that auto-threshold caps prevent >20% revenue leakage vs committed baseline.
2026-03-01 — Eng triage: billing pipeline changes scoped; ENG estimate is higher than expected due to legacy usage-aggregation windows. Proposed migration plan with shadow billing for 2 weeks.
2026-03-04 — Legal/Contracts: requested sample contract language for staircase pricing and clause for threshold abuse. Also flagged SAML customer audit requirements (added to QSA checklist).
2026-03-07 — Experiment design review: Data Science requested metric for 'effective vectors per rerank call' to ensure rerank bucket boundaries are meaningful. Added to experiment spec.
2026-03-10 — PM decision: move forward with 3-step tier design + auto-threshold (30d rolling) and rerank buckets (3). Kickoff billing prototype sprint next week.
